props.title: The Cincinnati Kid

sections.content: **The Cincinnati Kid** (1965) stands as one of the definitive poker films, setting the template that later classics like **Rounders** (1998) and **Molly's Game** (2017) would follow. Steve McQueen delivers a career-defining performance as Eric "The Kid" Stoner, a young poker prodigy trying to prove himself against Lancey "The Man" Howard (Edward G. Robinson). The film captures the sweaty, smoke-filled tension of high-stakes gambling in 1930s New Orleans, with director Norman Jewison using tight close-ups and methodical pacing to turn card playing into edge-of-your-seat drama. The Cincinnati Kid|1965|Steve McQueen stars as a young poker player challenging the reigning champion in Depression-era New Orleans|Prime Video Rounders|1998|Matt Damon and Edward Norton navigate the underground poker world of New York City|Netflix The Sting|1973|Two con men plot an elaborate revenge scheme using poker and horse racing|HBO Max

What sets **The Cincinnati Kid** apart is how it influenced the psychological thriller aspects of gambling films. Unlike later movies that relied on flashy techniques, Jewison keeps the focus tight on the psychological warfare between The Kid and The Man. This approach influenced films like **California Split** (1974) and **The Gambler** (1974), which similarly explore the addictive nature of gambling through character study rather than spectacle.

The film's legendary final poker scene became the blueprint for tense card showdowns, referenced in everything from **Casino Royale** (2006) to **Maverick** (1994). The way it builds tension through facial expressions and subtle gestures rather than dialogue demonstrates how powerful understated filmmaking can be. Hard Eight|1996|Philip Baker Hall mentors a young gambler in the ways of professional gambling|Criterion California Split|1974|Robert Altman's intimate look at two gambling addicts enabling each other|Tubi House of Games|1987|David Mamet's twisty thriller about a psychiatrist drawn into the world of con men|Prime Video SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Gambling Films

The influence of **The Cincinnati Kid** extends beyond just poker movies. Its exploration of mentorship and rivalry appears in films like **21** (2008) and **Mississippi Grind** (2015). The way it portrays gambling as a test of character rather than just luck has become a crucial element of the genre. Even non-gambling films like **The Color of Money** (1986) borrowed its master-versus-protégé dynamic.
